mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% is associated with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.5% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based expansion in supply capacity, which typically precedes higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.5% and HOUST > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST rise by more than 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate above 5% triggers market repricing of risk-free rates and equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps above 5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative after a single-month FEDFUNDS jump above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline of at least 1% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a synchronized contraction in demand, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -1% and RSAFS < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and RSAFS fall by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of at least 1% in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with a concurrent rise of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a supply-side contraction with labor market slack, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -1% and UNRATE > previous by 0.3pp in the same month
regime_hint: supply shock with labor market slack
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by at least 1% and UNRATE rises by at least 0.3pp in the same month.
